ky_practice_wall.blurb: A short sandstone cliff tucked into Joe Ponder Hollow within Muir Valley in the Red River Gorge. Most lines here are shorter than a typical gym wall, which makes it a gentle place to get a first feel for real rock. About two dozen routes, roughly two-thirds bolted and the rest trad, start at 5.1 and climb through the 5.7 to 5.9 range before reaching a handful of 5.10s, 5.11s and 5.12s. The easy lines suit top-roping with kids or a first lead, and there are a few harder pitches and a traverse for stronger climbers. Expect a relaxed, low-commitment outing rather than a destination day.

ky_5_undertow_wall.blurb: A long, steep wall at the Motherlode in the Red River Gorge, reached by the right-hand trail from the lot. It is the first cliff you meet and is overhanging and pumpy, with crimps, pockets, pinches and jugs rather than standout features. Roughly two dozen routes, nearly all bolted with a single trad line, cluster almost entirely in the 5.12 and 5.13 range, with only a couple of easier options near 5.10 and 5.11, so this is a place for strong climbers. The face stays mostly shaded during the day and picks up low evening light in the fall. A lower, less steep stretch lies off to the right of Madness Cave.
